title: Child Specifications, Restart Types (permanent/transient/temporary) & Shutdown Semantics
solutionExplanation: Constructs standardized child specification maps for workers and supervisors with shutdown => infinity protection, and implements the OTP Restart Type Truth Table.

otpDocCards.signature: child_spec() = #{id => term(), start => {M, F, A}, restart => restart(), shutdown => shutdown(), type => worker | supervisor, modules => [module()]}
otpDocCards.description: Map representation of a supervised child process, controlling start MFA, restart policy, shutdown timeout, and tree node type.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Static declarative specification compiled in supervisor init.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why does OTP require nested child supervisors to have shutdown => infinity instead of a numeric timeout like 5000?

options.label: A child supervisor needs sufficient time to terminate all of its own children in reverse order before it can exit; killing it prematurely leaves orphaned grandchild processes.
options.explanation: Supervisors must wait indefinitely for their children to finish terminating. The top-level application master manages the ultimate release shutdown timeout.

options.label: Erlang timers cannot run inside supervisor processes.
options.explanation: Supervisors can use timers; infinity is used to guarantee hierarchical clean shutdown without orphan leaks.

options.label: infinity makes the child process unkillable by OS signals.
options.explanation: OS signals kill the entire BEAM runtime; shutdown affects internal OTP supervisor exit signals.

options.label: numeric timeouts are only allowed on transient workers.
options.explanation: numeric timeouts are allowed on any worker process regardless of restart type.
